issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to an interface named 'Rideable' with method messageOnRide(), and the template Main.java also references Rideable. However, the solution repository introduces a different interface named 'Mountable' (with messageOnRide()) and the solution's Rideable.java is effectively empty. This name/type mismatch between the expected interface (Rideable) and the solution's Mountable will confuse students and graders: students following the problem statement will implement Rideable, but the solution shows Mountable, and the solution's Rideable file provides no definition.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the interface naming consistent. Either (A) rename Mountable.java to Rideable.java and have Pig and Seal implement Rideable (and ensure Rideable.java declares String messageOnRide()), or (B) update the problem statement and template comments to refer to Mountable instead of Rideable. Also remove or populate the empty Rideable.java in the solution so there is no stray, empty file.

issues.description: The exercise and template refer to an interface named 'Rideable' (with method messageOnRide()), but the solution implementation uses an interface named 'Mountable' and has classes (Pig, Seal) implement Mountable. This mismatched identifier for the same conceptual interface (ride/mount behavior) will confuse students: the problem text and template expect Rideable, while the solution code uses Mountable and leaves Rideable.java empty.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent interface name across all artifacts. Rename Mountable (and its file and references) to Rideable in the solution, implement the Rideable interface file with messageOnRide(), and ensure Pig and Seal implement Rideable. Alternatively, change the problem statement and template to use Mountable — but prefer aligning the solution to the problem's 'Rideable' identifier.
